hints.title: Consecutive Three Days Requirement
hints.text: A rolling average must only be calculated for dates that have records for today, yesterday, and the day before yesterday.

hints.title: Self Join Date Offsets
hints.text: Join the Steps table to itself twice on matching user_id with date differences of 1 and 2 days.

hints.title: Rounded Average
hints.text: Sum the three steps counts, divide by 3.0, round to 2 decimal places, and order by user_id ascending, steps_date ascending.

hints.title: Implementation
hints.text:
```sql
SELECT 
    s1.user_id,
    s1.steps_date,
    ROUND((s1.steps_count + s2.steps_count + s3.steps_count) / 3.0, 2) AS rolling_average
FROM Steps s1
JOIN Steps s2 ON s1.user_id = s2.user_id AND DATEDIFF(s1.steps_date, s2.steps_date) = 1
JOIN Steps s3 ON s1.user_id = s3.user_id AND DATEDIFF(s1.steps_date, s3.steps_date) = 2
ORDER BY s1.user_id ASC, s1.steps_date ASC;
```

variables: N: number of records in Steps table
complexity.notes: Self join on date offsets followed by sorting.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Window function avg over 2 preceding rows includes gaps across missing calendar days.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Enforce strict consecutive calendar day difference using self-join or range window.

SELECT 
    s1.user_id,
    s1.steps_date,
    ROUND((s1.steps_count + s2.steps_count + s3.steps_count) / 3.0, 2) AS rolling_average
FROM Steps s1
JOIN Steps s2 ON s1.user_id = s2.user_id AND (s1.steps_date - s2.steps_date) = 1
JOIN Steps s3 ON s1.user_id = s3.user_id AND (s1.steps_date - s3.steps_date) = 2
ORDER BY s1.user_id ASC, s1.steps_date ASC;

solutions.code:
import pandas as pd

def rolling_average(steps: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    steps["steps_date"] = pd.to_datetime(steps["steps_date"])
    steps = steps.sort_values(["user_id", "steps_date"])
    s2 = steps.copy()
    s2["date_plus_1"] = s2["steps_date"] + pd.Timedelta(days=1)
    s3 = steps.copy()
    s3["date_plus_2"] = s3["steps_date"] + pd.Timedelta(days=2)
    m1 = steps.merge(s2, left_on=["user_id", "steps_date"], right_on=["user_id", "date_plus_1"], suffixes=("", "_2"))
    m2 = m1.merge(s3, left_on=["user_id", "steps_date"], right_on=["user_id", "date_plus_2"], suffixes=("", "_3"))
    m2["rolling_average"] = ((m2["steps_count"] + m2["steps_count_2"] + m2["steps_count_3"]) / 3.0).round(2)
    res = m2[["user_id", "steps_date", "rolling_average"]].sort_values(["user_id", "steps_date"])
    res["steps_date"] = res["steps_date"].dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
    return res
solutions.approach: Pandas Merge on Consecutive Calendar Days
